title: The Afternoon Brief: Market rebounds on liquidations; whale flows decelerate
dek: Monday's tape shows Bitcoin rebounding sharply while leverage positions unwind, but the week-long outflow trend is slowing. Major altcoins staged broad gains against a backdrop of extreme fear.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
bottom_line: Monday rebounded on liquidations, with Bitcoin up 5.33% over 24 hours and altcoins posting broad gains, but spot Bitcoin ETF outflows of $669.2M on the day and $1,790.0M over the week show institutional selling persisted. The desk's Whale Watch board shows $452.9 million in bitcoin moving off exchanges over the week, the largest whale outflow, though the weekly trend has decelerated sharply from $4.1 billion the week of November 7 to $404 million the week ending November 21. Ether has reversed that pattern, with $177.6 million moving onto exchanges. Extreme Fear grips the market at an index reading of 11. The tape will test whether today's liquidation-driven rebound holds or whether outflows resume as leverage unwinds.
body: Monday's market action centered on a sharp intraday rebound across major crypto assets, driven by liquidation cascades that forced positions closed. Per the desk's leverage board, Bitcoin saw 100 liquidations in the last hour on OKX, with $719,962 in long positions closed. Bitcoin up 5.33% over 24 hours, while Ether up 7.23% over 24 hours, Solana up 10.67% over 24 hours, XRP up 9.93% over 24 hours, BNB up 5.01% over 24 hours, Dogecoin up 8.92% over 24 hours, and Cardano up 7.95% over 24 hours. Among the largest coins, QNT up 19.83% over 24 hours, ALGO up 15.62% over 24 hours, and LIT up 15.03% over 24 hours.

Despite the intraday strength, the broader trend remains under pressure. Bitcoin down 6.33% over seven days and down 24.57% over thirty days. Ether down 6.15% over seven days and down 27.81% over thirty days. Solana down 2.89% over seven days and down 31.27% over thirty days. XRP down 4.75% over seven days and down 28.29% over thirty days. BNB down 6.32% over seven days and down 24.37% over thirty days. Dogecoin down 12.41% over seven days and down 17.91% over thirty days. Cardano down 11.63% over seven days and down 25.13% over thirty days. The desk's market data shows Bitcoin at 48.8% below its twelve-month high of $124,739.81, while Ether sits 61.1% below its twelve-month peak of $4,690.84, underscoring the depth of the downtrend.

Monday's rebound did not arrest outflows from spot products. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $669.2M on the day, November 20, extending the outflow pattern into this week. Over the week through November 20, spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $1,790.0M. The cumulative position for spot Bitcoin ETF flows stands positive at $52,911.0 million, reflecting four consecutive days in the same direction through Friday last week; the latest session, however, reversed that momentum on the day.

The desk's Whale Watch board shows a more nuanced picture beneath the headline liquidations. Over the past week, $275,354,445 net moved off exchanges. Bitcoin accounted for $452,978,992 net moving off exchanges, the largest whale outflow by asset, with $318,720,651 moving off Kraken alone and $212,424,833 from the same venue in separate flows. Ethereum, however, reversed that pattern: $177,624,547 net moved onto exchanges, with $162,497,938 to Binance and $148,818,693 to Kraken. Stablecoins posted $77,862,597 net moving onto exchanges. The deceleration is visible in the weekly progression: the week ending November 7 saw $4,125 million moved off exchanges, the week ending November 14 saw $1,551 million, and the week ending November 21 saw $404 million. The current incomplete week ending November 28 shows $0 million so far.

Sentiment remains deeply depressed. The desk's Fear and Greed Index stands at 11, labeled Extreme Fear, the low end of its thirty-day range of 10 to 54. Bitcoin's RSI14 reads 36.0, below the neutral midpoint, while Ether's stands at 39.0. Per the desk's leverage board, Bitcoin funding on OKX stands calm at 0.0033% over eight hours, annualizing to 3.6%, while long-to-short ratios remain elevated at 2.3 for Bitcoin and 2.41 for Ethereum, leaving room for shorts to unwind further.
